meta.dataset_note: No entries with reference === 1112 AND type === 'bechina' exist in torahData.js. The dataset for LM2 currently extends only to reference 1105; Torah 112 (reference 1112) has not yet been entered into the dataset. The source text (torah_112.txt) is a single-sentence oral teaching about strengthening oneself (הִתְחַזְּקוּת) so as not to fall in one's mind because of the multitude of flaws and corruptions: 'If you believe that they can corrupt, believe that they can repair.' The word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear anywhere in the source text. There are no explicit bechina constructions ('X הוא בחינת Y', 'X נקרא Y') and no conceptual parallelism equating language. The teaching's sole rhetorical device is a symmetrical logical argument — if corrupting is possible, repairing is equally possible — which is a practical exhortation (eitza-type reasoning), not an ontological equation between concepts. Packages cannot be built from the bechina subgraph because the subgraph is empty.
